extracted.intended_audience: short-story writers, literary critics, editors, and informed readers
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and critical criteria for judging short stories and short-story collections (style, voice, unity, translation quality, economy, realism, mood, etc.), as used in an annual literary yearbook/review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Didactic intention subordinate to artistry
rubrics_metrics.description: Didactic or moral intention is acceptable only if kept entirely subordinate to the artistry of the exposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Mr. Aumonier has a certain didactic intention... he has kept it entirely subordinate to the artistry of his exposition.' Anti-pattern: letting an 'obvious moral' overwhelm narrative craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memorable characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters should be the lasting memory of a story, remaining with the reader after any moral or point has been conveyed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quote: 'it is the few characters which he has added to English fiction that we remember after his somewhat obvious moral has been conveyed.' Aim for characters that outlast plot or message.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent stylistic flavor
rubrics_metrics.description: A distinct, consistent stylistic 'flavor' (voice, period sensibility) can be a virtue when it suits the material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g., 'the same flavor of belated Victorianism' is praised when it reinforces the author's imaginative aims; consistency matters more than novelty for its own sake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentic observational realism
rubrics_metrics.description: Portraits of lives and local types should feel real even if the author did not live among those people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Pier studies... are none the less real because they are the product of observation by one who did not live among them.' Verisimilitude through careful observation is valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of condescension in depiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Portrayals of other peoples/regions should avoid a spirit of condescension and instead approach the subjects' heart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast given: a 'slight spirit of condescension' is a fault; works that 'approach far more closely to the heart' are praised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic infusion into prose
rubrics_metrics.description: Prose may be praised when it successfully conveys poetic sensibility—poetry for the mind within narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'she conveyed more poetry into "Irish Idylls" than into any other of her books.' Use of lyrical language that deepens rather than distracts is commended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustained imaginative world / animistic quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that create or sustain a convincing imaginative universe (animistic or otherwise) are highly valued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g., Blackwood 'has adequately maintained the quality of his best previous animistic work' — continuity and depth of imaginative vision matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passionate reality of portrayal
rubrics_metrics.description: Portrayals should have passion and reality—characters and scenes should feel vividly lived and emotionally present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited examples: stories 'hardly inferior... for their passionate reality.' The emotional truth of depiction strengthens literary value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent quality across a collection
rubrics_metrics.description: A volume should not contain weak items; uniformly strong stories make a better collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quote: 'There is no story in this volume which would not have made the reputation of a new writer.' Collections are judged on the reliability of their contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enduring beauty / timelessness
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that serves 'the altar of beauty' and promises increasing poignancy or influence over generations merits special praise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment considers whether an author's 'magic will gain greater poignancy as generations pass'—durability is a key criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of form (short story as true medium)
rubrics_metrics.description: The short story should be judged as the appropriate medium for what the author wants to do; some writers are better in short form than in novels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g., 'I suspect that the short story is her true literary medium.' Fit of subject and voice to form is an evaluative point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Range and variety of subject and mood
rubrics_metrics.description: A collection's capacity to span moods and subjects (e.g., tragedy to social comedy) is a positive attribute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a volume 'ranges from tragedy to social comedy'; variety demonstrates versatility and breadth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subtlety of irony (concealed irony)
rubrics_metrics.description: Irony should be subtle and not insistently evident—its concealment can increase effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quote: 'A subtle irony pervades them... so definitely concealed that its insistence is never evident.' Overt moralizing irony is an anti-pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vivid dramatic power and indigenous humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Narratives that capture local humor and dramatic vigor, rooted in their setting, are highly effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Bradley's 'racy humor' and 'vivid dramatic power' are praised; authenticity of regional voice is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic, unsparing portrayal of harsh subjects (e.g., war)
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers should be able to portray the 'naked ugliness' of experience (such as war) with the appropriate brutal power and passion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparison: Brooks' war stories are likened to 'The Red Badge of Courage'—truthful, unromantic depiction of brutality is a virtue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patterned prose and musical rhythmic speech
rubrics_metrics.description: Prose with pattern, musical rhythm, and the ability to find beauty in ugly things is laudable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g., Burke's 'patterned prose' and 'musical rhythmic speech' that soften stark horror into 'gracious beauty.' Craft of sentence-level rhythm matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation quality and idiomatic rendering
rubrics_metrics.description: Translations should be idiomatic, smooth, and capture subtle nuances of the original; poor idiomatic quality diminishes value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: Constance Garnett's translations praised for 'idiomatic speech and subtly rendered nuance'; other translations are critiqued as 'not thoroughly idiomatic.' Introductions/prefaces should not distract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique sufficient to author's purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Technique need not be flashy; it must be adequate and appropriate to achieve the author's intentions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quote: 'Their technique is sufficient for the author's purpose... he has achieved his will nobly in a manner inevitable to him.' Don't over-criticize technical simplicity if it serves purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full range of human emotion and spiritual observation
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that reflect the gamut of human feeling—from sublime tragedy to rich comedy—and offer spiritual observation are highly regarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation values works that 'range through the entire gamut of human emotion' and provide profound human insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity of speech and storytelling for its own sake
rubrics_metrics.description: A plain, simple telling that serves the story itself—'relates his story for the story's sake'—is a positive quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connolly praised for 'simplicity of speech' and telling stories plainly; avoid overwriting that calls attention to itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy of selection, description, and atmosphere
rubrics_metrics.description: Economy—tight selection of material, concise description, and economical emotional expression—produces dramatic quality and authenticity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple examples: 'utmost economy of speech', 'constant economy of selection', and Howells' exhortation toward 'descriptive and emotional economy.' Teach younger writers concision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craftsmanship combined with artistic humility
rubrics_metrics.description: Fine, vigorous craftsmanship presented with artistic humility (not ostentation) increases a work's value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corkery: 'A craftsmanship so fine and vigorous is seldom related with such artistic humility.' Humility in presentation enhances reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartial interest in character and vivid sense of landscape/spirit
rubrics_metrics.description: A writer's impartial interest in character and vivid spiritual valuation of landscape or setting strengthen the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cunningham Graham is praised for being 'more impartially interested in character' and having 'a far more vivid feeling for the spiritual values of landscape.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentic voice (ability to stand apart from influences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Work should possess an authentic voice that, while it may show influence, can stand on its own merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'the reader will detect in this book the authentic voice of Joseph Conrad' yet Curie 'can certainly afford to stand alone.' Balance influence and individuality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of incident / narrative compactness
rubrics_metrics.description: Even lengthy pieces can be short stories if they maintain an essential unity of incident and purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Machen: though 'as long as a short novel', it 'has an essential unity of incident which justifies... as a short story.' Unity matters more than length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation style: quiet, matter-of-fact tone to heighten tension
rubrics_metrics.description: A quiet, matter-of-fact narrative tone can increase emotional tension and realism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Machen's 'The Terror' uses a 'quiet matter-of-fact air' to enhance reader tension—restraint in tone can intensify effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial selection courage (including grim/unhappy endings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors should be willing to publish stories of 'grim quality' or unhappy endings; public interest may reward such choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'Grim Thirteen' anthology tested and rebutted an editorial bias against grim stories; experiment produced stories of 'permanent literary value.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact greater than range; careful selection to widen effect
rubrics_metrics.description: A collection's impact may exceed its formal range; selections should be chosen to maximize effect and influence readers/writers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Howells' note: 'The range of these stories is not very great; the effect they make is greater than the range.' Editors should select to amplify effect and teach economy.
